hook: Rice detects RNA fragments from stink bug saliva with a protein that forms condensates and triggers defense
summary: Sucking insects inject RNases that cut RNA into cyclic nucleotide fragments. The rice protein NIB1 binds these fragments, forms nuclear condensates, and recruits the immune regulator EDS1. Shown with genetics and biochemistry in rice and one insect species. The link to TIR protein signaling is only suggested.
title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2',3'-cNMP produced by insect effectors.
